# Test fixtures

`pdf/` is generated by `scripts/make-fixtures.ts` (`pnpm fixtures`). The script writes the PDFs by hand, uncompressed and without timestamps, so the output is reproducible; a unit test fails if the committed files differ from what the script makes.

| File               | What it is                                                                 | Expected result               |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `multi-page.pdf`   | 4 text pages, `/Title` "Quarterly Report 2026", blank lines between blocks | extracts; title from metadata |
| `french.pdf`       | accents, œ, curly quotes, and the ﬁ ﬂ ﬀ ﬃ ﬄ ligatures as glyph names       | plain letters, accents kept   |
| `hyphenation.pdf`  | words split across lines, plus hyphens that must stay                      | `informa-` + `tion` is joined |
| `image-only.pdf`   | one page with a picture and no text                                        | `pdf_no_text`                 |
| `partial-text.pdf` | text, picture, text                                                        | extracts; page 2 is empty     |
| `encrypted.pdf`    | RC4 40-bit, user password `secret`, owner password `owner`                 | `pdf_encrypted`               |
| `owner-only.pdf`   | same encryption, empty user password (print/copy restricted)               | extracts                      |
| `corrupted.pdf`    | `%PDF-1.4` header followed by noise                                        | `pdf_corrupted`               |
| `renamed-text.pdf` | plain text saved with a .pdf name                                          | `pdf_not_pdf`                 |
| `empty.pdf`        | a valid PDF with zero pages                                                | `pdf_no_text`                 |

The 2,001-page and 2,000-page files for the page-cap tests are built in memory by `buildBlankPages()` in the same script, not committed.

`encrypted.pdf` is a real encrypted file, made by implementing the standard security handler (revision 2: MD5 and RC4, PDF 1.7 section 7.6.3) in the script, because no PDF tool such as qpdf is needed or assumed. `fixtures.test.ts` checks that pdf.js refuses it without the password and reads it with `secret`.
